newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia defends mining policy after Busang.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia defends mining policy after Busang.

text.p: Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana on Wednesday defended Indonesia's mining policy, saying critics were confused and lacked proper understanding.

"They say our mining policy is unconstitutional and has neglected our national interests. This clearly shows a lack of proper understanding," he told a gathering of the Indonesia- Canada Chamber of Commerce in Jakarta.

Sudjana did not refer to any particular issue, but was believed to be hitting out at those who had voiced dissatisfaction over the government's handling of the huge Busang gold find in East Kalimantan province.
The government had ordered Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd, which discovered the deposit, to partner Barrick Gold Corp to jointly develop the property.
But the two companies said they were unable to reach an agreement, leading to Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc of the United States replacing Barrick.

The government last week announced it had approved an agreement under which Bre-X will hold a 45 percent stake in the property, PT Askatindo Karya Minerals and PT Amsya Lyna and their partners 30 percent, Freeport 15 percent and the Indonesian government the remaining 10 percent.

The Nusamba group, headed by Muhammad "Bob" Hasan, holds 50 percent stakes in PT Askatindo and PT Amsya. The Nusamba group, in turn, is 80 percent owned by three foundations headed by President Suharto.
Bre-X estimates the property contains some 71 million ounces of gold currently worth $24 billion.
Indonesia was fully committed to continuing with its mining policy that conformed with the constitution, Sudjana said.
He also said the recent spate of social unrest in the country had had no negative impact on the economy.
"You might have noticed in the press the occurrence of some unrest here and there. Ethnic, religious and other social discrepancies have always been used as battlefields for political practitioners.
"Taking into account all these political noises, I would like to assure you that this is only a very short-term phenomenon. A small wave during this rainy season," he said.
"After each democratic festival or election, political stability returns by its own into our daily life," he said.
Indonesia has been rocked by several ethnic and religious clashes since the middle of last year.
